title: Straight Lines: Slope, Forms of the Equation and Distance
seo_title: Straight Lines Class 11 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 9)
standard_text: Brief recall of two dimensional geometry from earlier classes; slope of a line and angle between two lines; various forms of equations of a line: parallel to axis, point-slope form, slope-intercept form, two-point form and intercept form; distance of a point from a line (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 11 Straight Lines worksheet (NCERT Chapter 9): slope, inclination, parallel and perpendicular lines, angle between lines, collinearity, forms of the equation and distance from a line. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Distance from (x₁, y₁) to ax + by + c = 0 is |ax₁ + by₁ + c|/√(a² + b²).
body_html:
How it works

  • Slope m = (y2 − y1) ÷ (x2 − x1) = tan θ, where θ is the inclination.
  • Parallel lines: m1 = m2. Perpendicular lines: m1m2 = −1. Angle: tan θ = |(m2 − m1) ÷ (1 + m1m2)|.
  • Forms: y − y1 = m(x − x1); y = mx + c; x/a + y/b = 1.
  • Distance of (x1, y1) from Ax + By + C = 0: |Ax1 + By1 + C| ÷ √(A² + B²).
Example

Find the distance of (3, −5) from 3x − 4y − 26 = 0.

|9 + 20 − 26| ÷ √(9 + 16)

= 3 ÷ 5

Answer: 3/5

Common mistakes

  • Using (x₂ − x₁)/(y₂ − y₁) for the slope.
  • Saying perpendicular lines have m₁m₂ = 1.
  • Leaving out the modulus or the square root in the distance.
